scope: Tape briefings for players aged 9-12: what the room is for and its two repairs, by their action titles (UI overhaul, 2026-11-15).

cassettes.title: Command center
pages: This is the Command Room. From here the colony talks to Mission Control. The storm knocked out the radio signal and pulled the relay cables loose.
Lock the Relay: anyone can turn the knob until the two waves match. Patch the Relay: only the Electrical specialist can plug each cable into its shape.
cassettes.caption: NASA astronaut Jonny Kim uses a ham radio to speak with students from the International Space Station. This is ISS communications, not a Mars control room.

cassettes.title: Power supply
pages: The Power Room stores the Sun's power in a big battery, so the base has light at night. Its turbine and its power bench both need fixing.
Sync the Turbine: anyone can stop each ring in the green. Light the Power Bench: only the Electrical specialist can make a path to the lamp.
cassettes.caption: Solar arrays on the Russian segment of the International Space Station, photographed by an Expedition 38 crew member on February 5, 2014. Earth is visible beyond the station.

cassettes.title: Greenhouse
pages: The Greenhouse grows the colony's food. Plants need light, water and plant food. A water pipe broke, so the kale is dry.
Water the Kale: anyone can turn the pipes until water reaches the plants. The Agriculture specialist looks after the plant food.
cassettes.caption: Radishes growing in the Plant Habitat-02 experiment aboard the International Space Station, photographed on November 11, 2020. The chamber supports controlled plant-growth research.

cassettes.title: Green dome
pages: The Garden Dome is a big glass room full of plants. Its glass keeps the air inside. One window pane cracked and needs new glass.
Glaze the Dome: anyone can fit the five glass pieces into the window. The Field engineer looks after the dome's pipes.
cassettes.caption: A NASA Advanced Plant Habitat engineering development unit at Kennedy Space Center in Florida, 2016. This photographed ground prototype is an engineering analogy, not a Martian garden dome.

cassettes.title: Med Bay
pages: The Med Bay keeps the crew healthy. The lab samples got mixed up, and two machines lost their power.
Sort the Lab Samples: only the Medical specialist can pour each shape into its own tube. Revive the Med Bay: anyone can plug the machines back in.
cassettes.caption: NASA astronaut Chris Cassidy performs an ultrasound on ESA astronaut Luca Parmitano in the ISS Columbus laboratory on August 21, 2013. This is medical research, not a game reagent recipe.

cassettes.title: Hangar / airlock
pages: The Hangar holds the rover, and the airlock is the door to the outside. Dust covers the landing lines, and the airlock is leaking air.
Clear the Landing Lines: anyone can brush and vacuum the dust away. Seal the Airlock: only the Field engineer can fit the new seal.
cassettes.caption: NASA astronaut Michael Hopkins prepares tools and U.S. spacesuits inside the ISS Quest airlock on December 17, 2020. This is real ISS suit staging, not a fictional Mars leak repair.
